maker: University of Pennsylvania (J. Presper Eckert, John Mauchly) for the US Army
summary: The first programmable, general-purpose electronic digital computer, built at the University of Pennsylvania for the US Army to calculate artillery tables. It filled a room with 17,000 vacuum tubes and was programmed by six women who rewired it by hand.

image.alt: Two programmers setting up ENIAC’s panels in 1946

events.note: The Army signs the contract to build it.

events.label: First use
events.note: Runs its first real job, calculations for Los Alamos.
Formally dedicated at the University of Pennsylvania.

events.label: Aberdeen
events.note: Switched back on after moving to the Army’s Aberdeen Proving Ground.

image.alt: Glen Beck and Betty Snyder programming ENIAC at the Ballistic Research Laboratory
image.caption: ENIAC in building 328 of the Ballistic Research Laboratory.

events.label: Stored program
events.note: First runs as a stored-program computer.
Parts of it are on display at the University of Pennsylvania and in museums.

image.alt: Two ENIAC panels on display at the University of Pennsylvania
image.caption: Panels on display at Penn’s Moore School.

cause: Switched off for good after nearly ten years of service.
